heading: INT. UNDERGROUND CURLING CLUB - SHEET THREE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. UNDERGROUND CURLING CLUB - SHEET THREE - NIGHT
A converted subway platform.
Tile walls, strip lights, a stripe of imported ice laid down over concrete.
Condensation drips from the ceiling in a slow clock.
The air smells of coffee and old wool.
Four players and a referee stand at the hog line, brooms in hand.
NIKOLAI "KOLYA" ARSENIEV (50s, skip, cardigan, spine like a steel rod) crouches at the house, tapping the ice with his broom.
PADMA IYENGAR (30s, lead, ponytail, scrappy) is on the far hack, stone ready.
TEODORO "TEDDY" BRAVO (40s, second, sweaty, gold chain on top of his jersey) hovers behind her, nervous as a bridegroom.
JUNE ASHBY-LANE (20s, vice, lean, focused in a way that seems to cost her) holds her broom like a rifle.
Off to the side, REFEREE OKONKWO (60s, whistle, immaculate blazer) writes on a clipboard.
Padma. Draw to the button. Light.
units.name: KOLYA

units.text: Light, Kolya.
units.name: PADMA

units.text: Don't throw it like it owes you money.
units.name: KOLYA

units.text: It does owe me money.
units.name: PADMA

units.text: It owes all of us, Padma. Throw the thing.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: She slides.
The stone leaves her hand with a long grinding hum.
Kolya and June sweep in step, their brooms hissing.
The stone rolls, curls, drifts into the rings.
Hard! Hard! Hard!
units.name: JUNE

units.text: Off, off, it's fine, let it go!
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: The stone dies.
Sits on the edge of the button.
Perfect.
Padma rises out of her slide, grinning.
Teddy claps his hands once, then covers his mouth, as if he'd been caught laughing in church.
Measure.
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: He kneels and lays a plastic gauge across the stone.
A hush.
Drops of condensation tick on the ice.
That is the match.
units.name: KOLYA

units.text: Eleven millimetres to the opposition.
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: Kolya exhales.
Teddy turns in a circle.
June does not smile.
She stares at her teammates and the smile she can't produce seems to push at the corners of her eyes.
Teddy.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: What?
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: You touched the stone.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: Everyone stops.
I didn't.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Your sleeve. Your sleeve brushed the stone as it passed.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: Kolya, tell her.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Teodoro.
units.name: KOLYA

units.text: It was the draught!
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Sheet three, burned stone. It comes off.
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: You cannot be serious.
units.name: PADMA

units.text: Then take it off.
units.name: ^JUNE

units.text: They speak together, flat and angry, over each other.
Okonkwo does not blink.
He picks the stone up with both hands and carries it off the ice.
Kolya takes off his glasses.
Folds them.
Slips them into the cardigan pocket as though he were closing a funeral.
Five years of Thursdays.
units.name: KOLYA

units.text: He turns and walks the length of the sheet.
The brooms fall one by one behind him.
Teddy's is the last, and it makes the loudest sound.
FADE OUT.
